correctness.rationale: The rational iterate is exactly \(f_{p/q,\phi}^q(x,y)=(x,y+\Phi_q(x))\), and polynomial entropy is unchanged by positive iterates. For a scalar twist \(G_\psi(u,v)=(u,v+\psi(u))\) with continuous \(\psi\) on compact \(K\), fix a finite small-diameter base cover and a fixed fiber net, then partition the bounded velocity interval into \(O(n)\) bins of width \(O(1/n)\). Points chosen in the same base patch and velocity bin remain uniformly close for all times up to \(n\), yielding an \(O(n)\) spanning set and \(h_{\mathrm{pol}}(G_\psi)\le1\) without any modulus-of-continuity assumption. If \(\psi\) is constant the twist is an isometry. If \(\psi:\mathbb T\to\mathbb R\) is nonconstant, its rotation set contains an interval and Corrêa's 2026 theorem gives the matching lower bound \(h_{\mathrm{pol}}\ge1\).
residual_risks: The result exposes an apparent contradiction with the published 2023 \(\omega(r)=|r|^\alpha\) claim; the current online article still displays that claim.

originality.rationale: Corrêa computes the rational iterate and rotation set and proves the lower bound when \(\Phi_q\) is nonconstant, but his scalar upper bound assumes Lipschitz regularity. The assigned velocity-range covering removes that hypothesis by a genuinely different organization of spanning points and yields the exact continuous classification. The closest broader 2023 fibered-system result instead states a Hölder-dependent value \(1/\alpha\) for \(\omega(r)=|r|^\alpha\), which conflicts with the new universal scalar-twist upper bound rather than covering it. No implication-equivalent Resultary record was found beyond the assigned result.
residual_risks: The 2023 Springer page notes that the article has been updated, but the current displayed text still contains the conflicting \(1/\alpha\) proposition and no separate correction resolving it was located.
